podcast.body: This song established Donna Summer as the "queen of Disco" and became renowned for its explicit pushing of boundaries in female sexual expression. Initially 3 minutes and 50 seconds, Neil Bogart requested a longer version after witnessing its impact at a party, leading to the iconic 17-minute track. Donna Summer reportedly recorded the song's sensual vocal moans and breathing in a dark booth, lying on the floor, due to her self-consciousness. Bogart himself noted its appeal as music "for people who just want to sit and relax and make love." "The song that made her the queen is love to love you, baby."
